source.title: ResMem: Learn what you can and memorize the rest
source.authors: Zi-Tong Yang; Michal Lukasik; Vaishnavh Nagarajan; Zong-xiao Li; A. S. Rawat; M. Zaheer; A. Menon; Surinder Kumar

record.tranche_reason: Applies explicit residual memorization to small image classifiers and autoregressive language models, and reports effects on test performance and training/test accuracy in a new setting relative to the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates a residual k-NN augmentation, not the listed architectures, optimizer, batch-size, explicit-regularization, size, or sharpness conditions as causes of the natural-label generalization gap. Its CIFAR100 sample-size figures compare training and test accuracy, and its experiments report test-accuracy changes from adding residual memorization. Random-label fitting is discussed only as cited prior work; it is not tested here.
record.test_reason: The study uses prior work linking memorization and generalization to motivate ResMem and reports its own method's performance. It does not test any of V1–V8: explicit residual storage is neither random-label fitting by the same neural training recipe nor removal of examples selected by influence-based memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report improved held-out performance from explicit residual k-NN memorization and posit the largest benefits when implicit memorization is infeasible. Their coarse-to-fine explanation is supported by qualitative examples, rather than established as a causal mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The study adds a separate residual k-NN component after training the base model; it does not test the original interventions or measurements in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported gains vary with base-model architecture, CIFAR100 training-set fraction, and training epoch. The study reports a unimodal test-accuracy response to ResMem σ and temperature T; accuracy is relatively stable across k values tested.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual k-NN augmentation improves reported held-out accuracy on CIFAR100, C4, and ImageNet; improvements generally grow with dataset size and shrink with model size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding a residual k-NN predictor can improve a neural model's held-out accuracy, particularly for smaller models and larger datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: ResMem corrects more baseline errors than it introduces errors on previously correct examples in the reported CIFAR100 and C4 decompositions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual retrieval can produce a net accuracy gain while also damaging some correct baseline predictions.

fits_no_version.finding: ResMem improves accuracy at every reported CIFAR-ResNet-8 stopping epoch, with the largest gain at epoch 128.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual retrieval can improve the held-out accuracy of an incompletely trained base network.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 3.3 gives a vanishing test-risk bound for residual nearest-neighbor augmentation of norm-constrained linear regression in a noiseless stylized setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A nonparametric residual component can overcome approximation error in a constrained parametric predictor under the theorem's assumptions.

record.problems: The principal test-accuracy plots do not provide exact values for each architecture or training-data fraction in the supplied text. Statistical variability is reported only for the five-run CIFAR-ResNet-8 experiment. The language experiment uses 1% of the C4 training split as its retrieval database, with approximate nearest-neighbor search.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The cited random-label and generalization findings in related work are not results of this study.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting experiment or natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison using the same neural architecture and training recipe.
No width sweep past an established zero-training-error threshold. ResNet depth and pretrained MobileNet width comparisons do not establish this condition.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or intervention on local connectivity or initialization.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison under specified tuning budgets.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adaptation of a large-batch recipe.
No dropout intervention. Appendix E's fixed dropout rate is a training detail.
No magnitude-aware weight perturbation measure, gap-ranking analysis, or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples, random-removal control, or retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: States describe assessability against V1–V8; cannot_determine does not dispute the reported method gains. No missing result bears on a listed version. Random-label fitting and influence-based memorization appear as prior-work motivation. ResMem's hyperparameter sensitivity and additional baseline comparisons concern its own performance.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
No width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch penalty test.
No dropout intervention or dropout/weight-decay removal comparison.
No sharpness or generalization-gap measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples or retraining comparison.

rows.operation_detail: Added residual k-NN predictor to the base network using pre-logit embeddings; CIFAR100 test accuracy comparison.
rows.note: The paper reports this as a 3.19% test-accuracy gain in Section 4.4.
rows.check: Own-method performance comparison; exclude from claim-evidence rows. Values match Section 4.2. The 3.20 percentage-point difference differs slightly from Section 4.4's 3.19.

rows.note: These are reported average accuracies across five runs.
rows.check: Own-method performance comparison; exclude from claim-evidence rows. Five-run means and standard deviations match the text.

rows.subject: CIFAR-ResNet-8
rows.operation_detail: Added residual k-NN predictor and compared accuracy across training-set fractions.
rows.measure: test accuracy and training accuracy by sample fraction
rows.note: The text says ResMem yields progressively larger margins of improvement with more data and always achieves perfect training accuracy; precise per-fraction values appear only in the figure.
rows.check: Own-method sample-size comparison; exclude from claim-evidence rows. Combines training and test accuracy across multiple conditions. Perfect training accuracy is engineered through explicit retrieval and does not establish V1's random-label comparison.
